chunk_findings.detail: The `clock-env` family is mapped to the entire `os` root module, although the stated family is time/uuid/random/os.environ. Because `_external_roots` records only import roots, any module that does `import os` or `from os import path` for `os.path` is placed in `clock-env.importers`; since `clock-env` has no declared home, `FamilyReport.violations` lists it. For example, adding `ddflow/foo.py` containing `import os` and using `os.path.join("a", "b")` makes `ddflow.foo` a `clock-env` violation even though it never touches `os.environ`. This misclassifies ordinary path use as clock/env/randomness dependency and can make the ratchet baseline grow for code that should not belong to the `clock-env` family.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archdeps.py:37

chunk_findings.detail: `_external_roots` swallows `SyntaxError` and `OSError` and returns no imports. A file that cannot be parsed or read is silently treated as having no dependencies, so a forbidden import in that file is invisible to the census. For example, create `ddflow/foo.py` containing `import subprocess` followed by a syntax error such as `def f(:`; `_external_roots` catches the `SyntaxError` and returns `()`, so `scan(repo)` reports no `subprocess` importer and no violation, allowing a new importer outside the family’s home to evade the ratchet. The census should fail or report the unparsable/unreadable file rather than omit it from the dependency census.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archdeps.py:101-104

chunk_findings.detail: The command registers itself under `tool="ddflow_archdeps"`, i.e. a new tool named after the command, even though the stated intent and D-unify require this to be an action on the existing tool/view surface (consistent with `family="ddflow_view"` and `help_group="view"`). Loading `COMMANDS` therefore either fails registry validation against the existing tool set or creates a second tool; in either case the `archdeps` action is not added to the existing tool’s action surface, violating the strangler/ratchet requirement [D-unify].

chunk_findings.detail: The ratchet test cannot enforce “baseline ignore lists only shrink” because it compares the scan against the same editable `BASELINE` literal in the test file. Given a change that adds a new module outside a family’s declared home, e.g. `ddflow.foo` importing `sqlite3` outside `ddflow.infra.docindex`, and the same change appends `"ddflow.foo"` to `BASELINE["sqlite3"]`, `test_ratchet_violations_match_baseline` sees `got == want` and passes; `test_default_scan_reports_every_family` also passes because `"sqlite3"` is already in the family set, and `test_violations_are_importers_outside_the_home` still passes for `http`-style no-home families because violations equal importers. This contradicts the stated ratchet requirement that a new importer outside a home fails and that baselines only shrink.
